races.name: Follow @attheraces On X Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hamdani Mokhater
runners_data.note: Won at Lingfield AW over 8f on Standard previously (sim-going 1 win from 6) and steps back here; Jack Mitchell retains, but the hold-up style leaves him dependent on the pace faltering, and recent form reads 5-7-5-2-3 — consistent without threatening.|
runners_data.comment: Hamdani Mokhater shaped with promise when third two starts back and runner-up three starts back, and our rating of 75 ranks him second in this field, making him a clear danger despite that disappointing seventh last time out.

runners_data.name: Bollengo Boy
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton runner whose best AW run was a second over this course and trip on Standard, giving him a legitimate angle; however his natural hold-up style means he cannot get into the position he wants here, racing out of role in a field stacked with closers, and his form over shorter on Good has been weak.|
runners_data.comment: Bollengo Boy shaped well when runner-up last time out and has run over today's trip, while his rating of 70 suggests he holds strong claims from stall one; the main concern is a trainer in poor nick, striking at just 3% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Galore
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the ride on a Michael Bell juvenile who has finished 9th, 5th and 8th in three starts — all on Good — and the fade flag is a concern as he steps to a mile for the first time; bumped back into midfield from his natural rear position, his chance is structurally compromised.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Whiskey Galore faces a stiff task off 129 lb from stall 10, though he has run over today's trip before and returns on a reasonable 28-day break.

runners_data.name: Magical Life
runners_data.note: The one hold-up runner with a genuine winning entry on this surface (1 win from 8f AW Standard), making him the strongest candidate among the closers; Moore's yard is 3 from 15 in the last 14 days and Ghiani knows how to ride the track, but ten days between runs and a STYLE_FIT flag temper expectations.|
runners_data.comment: Magical Life won two starts back and returns on a sharp ten-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going in her favour, carrying 128 lb from stall 11; the worry is that her latest fourth suggests she may need to find more to follow up.

runners_data.name: Kiss Cam
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon rides for Richard Hughes but three runs show 6th, 6th, 11th with sim-going record of 0 wins from 3 at Lingfield Standard; wears a hood, and though that can sharpen a juvenile, the form is deeply uninspiring and the hold-up style serves her poorly here.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, Kiss Cam faces a stiff task from stall seven carrying 128 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 61 suggests she holds a shade more ability than her official mark implies.

runners_data.name: Goblet
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison sends out a horse returning after 52 days — the longest break in the field — with a fade flag attached and a best AW run of only 4th; Rob Hornby takes over in the saddle but the horse's form trajectory (12th, 4th, 8th) is not encouraging and the layoff adds risk.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked eighth of eleven on our ratings, Goblet at least has experience of today's trip and going to call upon, though 52 days off and a fourth and eighth in recent outings suggest improvement is needed.

runners_data.name: Allaboutthelunch
runners_data.note: A lightly-weighted 45-rated juvenile for Edward Smyth-Osbourne whose record reads 12th, 9th, 9th, 5th — all modest — and the 5lb claimer Olivia Tubb takes the ride; not placed once in four starts and the fade flag makes a mile on AW a tough ask.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with a pair of ninths and a fifth among those efforts, Allaboutthelunch is hard to fancy ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a reasonable 17-day break.

runners_data.name: Hailstones In May
runners_data.note: Tyler Heard partners this Richard Hughes-trained filly whose three runs returned 12th, 8th and 6th — all on Good — and who has never raced on AW; the step up to a mile is unknown territory, the fade flag is prominent, and 42 days off adds further uncertainty.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked towards the foot of our figures, Hailstones In May faces a stiff ask here, with nothing in his recent form — two finishes deep in the field — to inspire confidence, though 42 days off may have freshened him.

runners_data.name: No More Pino
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner and therefore the pivotal horse for pace shape; Charlie Pike's yard is 0 from 7 in the past 14 days and the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that No More Pino is mapped as Prominent rather than a confirmed wire-to-wire type, but with no rival to press him, Levey has every chance to control fractions over this trip.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, No More Pino nonetheless rates top of these on our figures and returns quickly on just eight days' rest; he has run over today's trip before and carries 135 lb from stall two.

runners_data.name: Prince Kameo
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's patient handling of juveniles is well-documented and this horse has placed (4th, 4th) at AW Standard before; Jack Gilligan gets the nod and of all the hold-up horses, Kameo is most likely to take a forward position by default, making him one of the better-placed runners for the dominant scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Prince Kameo at least has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 26 days between runs leaves him fresh enough; the 134 lb burden is the obvious concern for a gelding rated 64 trying to break that duck.

runners_data.name: Ten Of Clubs
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and shaped with a placed run on AW Standard over 8f most recently (3rd), suggesting he handles the surface; Saffie Osborne is booked for Jamie Osborne, and the horse's AW form — 3rd, 8th, 8th — makes him one of the more credible hold-up types to grab a prominent spot if the field strings out early.|
runners_data.comment: Ten Of Clubs returns on a quick 17-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and conditions in his favour, and that third last time out offers a crumb of encouragement; yet winless in his last four starts and carrying 131 lb from stall nine, he faces a stiff ask against stronger rivals.

races.paceDynamic: No More Pino is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner nursery handicap over Lingfield's polytrack mile, and with no genuine pace rival to challenge him, Sean Levey can dictate a controlled, sustainable tempo from the outset. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types — Bollengo Boy, Whiskey Galore, Magical Life, Kiss Cam, Goblet, Allaboutthelunch, Hailstones In May, Prince Kameo, Ten Of Clubs and Hamdani Mokhater all want to race off the pace — meaning the bulk of the field will be chasing one leader rather than forcing him into a genuine test. This field holds far more hold-up horses than the map can honestly place at the rear; of those with any chance of actually tracking closer to the pace, Prince Kameo (Sir Mark Prescott, patient buildup) and Ten Of Clubs (shown early pace in AW form) are the most likely to occupy a prominent berth in the slipstream by default. The race shape strongly favours No More Pino and any horse able to sit just off him in second or third, as a single-pace gallop over a mile on Standard Polytrack will rarely be run fast enough to reel in a relaxed front-runner who controls his own fractions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If No More Pino bowls along uncontested and sets a fair but controlled tempo, turning for home with a decisive lead.
scenarios.body: No More Pino can graduate to a mile having run over shorter, and with no rival willing or able to push him, Levey can produce him fresh and balanced into the straight; horses who settle just behind him in second or third — absorbing his fractions rather than chasing from deep — are best placed to pounce if he tires.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Ten Of Clubs or Prince Kameo secure prominent positions immediately behind No More Pino and the leader ties up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A modest leader who has been lightly raced at the mile trip could flatten out approaching the Lingfield straight, handing the advantage to a horse who has sat in second or third throughout and needs only a length or two to pounce; both Ten Of Clubs and Prince Kameo have the AW mile form to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If No More Pino sets an uncharacteristically strong early pace or ties up markedly turning in, opening the door for a well-timed late run.
scenarios.body: Magical Life is the most credible hold-up racer in the field, having won over this course and distance at Standard and finishing placed at Lingfield previously, giving Ghiani a genuine pattern to follow; Hamdani Mokhater also arrives in form and could benefit if ground is given late, though most redistributed hold-up types will struggle to bridge the gap from deep.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If No More Pino sets a crawl that compresses the field and produces a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A muddling gallop would theoretically suit closers, but the majority of this field's hold-up runners carry significant form concerns — multiple fade flags, poor AW sim-going records, and redistributed positioning — meaning even a truly end-to-end sprint may not deliver a clean result from the back; Bollengo Boy and Whiskey Galore, natural hold-up horses who find themselves mapped into midfield, would need this shape most but are least likely to translate it into victory given their current form.

watchPoints.text: No More Pino's early sectionals are critical — if Levey allows him to drift into a very slow pace, the bunched field becomes a lottery and his lead evaporates; watch whether he is actively managed or allowed to coast.

Prince Kameo and Ten Of Clubs are both likely to push forward from their draw to occupy the positions immediately behind the leader — if both do so aggressively, a minor pace battle could develop in the first two furlongs despite the apparent lack of front-runners.

Magical Life is the hold-up horse with the most legitimate AW form claim; if Ghiani finds an unimpeded route along the inner turning for home, he is the likeliest beneficiary of any late collapse from the front.

The fade flags on Whiskey Galore, Goblet, Allaboutthelunch, Hailstones In May and Ten Of Clubs collectively suggest the field's stamina is fragile — if the pace is genuinely strong, attrition in the final two furlongs could be significant.

Trainer Richard Hughes has two runners (Kiss Cam and Hailstones In May) in the field — neither has convincing form but watch for any market move on either, which could indicate stable confidence in one runner over the other.

races.name: Celebrate National Racehorse Week Maiden Fillies' Stakes (gbb/gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Kiah
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Brian Meehan with Tom Marquand aboard, ran twice at Goodwood on good ground and showed enough to be placed second; steps up to a mile for the first time and gets a flat, uncontested-or-contested lead here depending on how Boomshakalak travels — that energy duel is her biggest risk.

runners_data.name: Please Don't Go
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes over for Richard Hughes, whose yard is in reasonable nick at 4/28 in the past fortnight; settled hold-up style suits a truly-run pace and the AW mile, with a sim-going record of one run but no wins or places on this surface to point to — improvement needed.

runners_data.name: Scrappetalene
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's lightly raced filly (just one run, fifth at Goodwood over 7f on good) carries significant unknown quantity given her minimal profile; Rob Hornby can't give us much of a steer on style, so she is treated as uncertain, making her difficult to assess but not dismissible if there is raw ability lurking.

runners_data.name: Thuritha
runners_data.note: Consistent without threatening in two starts for David Simcock — fifth both times over 7f, once on Lingfield AW Standard which is the most relevant bit of form here; Sean Levey takes the ride and will need a step forward from a hold-up position if the closers are to beat the pace.

runners_data.name: Boomshakalak
runners_data.note: Zoe Hawkins's runner has been off 50 days since a single seventh-place run over 7f at Goodwood, so fitness is a mild query; a confirmed front-runner who will push Kiah for the lead, and the distance step to a mile on AW may or may not suit — her involvement in a pace duel makes her as likely to set the race up for others as to win it herself.

races.paceDynamic: Kiah and Boomshakalak are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from the outset over this Lingfield AW mile, creating a genuinely competitive gallop from the first furlong rather than a dawdle. With two horses pressing each other through the early stages, the pace is likely to be honest rather than manufactured, stretching the field and ensuring the race is run at a true tempo. The hold-up runners Please Don't Go and Thuritha will settle in behind the pace, while Scrappetalene's style is uncertain but she is likely to find a mid-division berth. This race shape — two pace-setters burning off each other — classically favours horses who can travel in behind a genuine gallop and produce a sustained late run, making the hold-up and midfield profiles the primary beneficiaries once the front two stop racing each other.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Two Fight, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Kiah and Boomshakalak press each other through the first half of the race at an honest clip, leaving them vulnerable in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The contested pace sets up a truly-run mile that will expose any weaknesses in the leaders, bringing the hold-up horses into play with a clear run from the home turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Softens, Leader Steals
scenarios.trigger: If Boomshakalak settles and Kiah concedes position early, allowing one front-runner to control a steadier gallop.
scenarios.body: A single leader controlling an uncontested moderate pace can conserve energy and prove surprisingly hard to reel in around Lingfield's tight final bend.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Pick-Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Scrappetalene travels smoothly in mid-division and produces an untapped burst from a horse still well short of full exposure.
scenarios.body: Lightly raced and with only one outing, Scrappetalene carries genuine improvement potential, and a truly-run pace that spreads the field could allow a clean run from the inside.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Fails To Quicken
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses into a falsely-run race and the hold-up horses are left with too much ground to make up in a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A muddling gallop suits those who can sit handy and kick, making it hard for the back-markers to land a telling blow over this Lingfield mile.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Kiah or Boomshakalak clears the other in the first two furlongs — if neither gives way, both could be weakened by halfway and gift the race to the hold-up runners.

Please Don't Go holds the strongest trainer-jockey combination on form (Hughes/Fallon, 4/28 strike rate) and could be the primary beneficiary if the pace scenario unfolds as expected — watch her positioning off the final bend.

Scrappetalene's unknown style and lightly raced profile (just one run) means she could travel anywhere in the field; jockey choice and early positioning will be highly informative when the stalls open.

Boomshakalak returns from a 50-day break having run just once — monitor her market movement late on, as any fitness doubt could see her connections reluctant to force the pace aggressively, which would fundamentally alter the race shape.

All five fillies carry 128lbs on Standard AW going — no weight or surface differential to separate them, so early pace configuration and how each horse handles the Lingfield left-hand bend into the straight will be the key race-reading factor.

runners_data.name: General Assembly
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two recent second-place finishes on this surface at this trip (2/5f/STA twice), giving solid place claims, though a trainer in 0/1 form over 14 days and 47 days off the track are minor cautions; will be first or second into stride and sets the tempo.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, General Assembly nonetheless brings distance and going experience to the table and his speed rating of 75 outstrips his official mark — a case can be made for him outrunning expectations from stall four carrying 130 lb, though his recent consistency is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Mick's Spirit
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old prominent racer with strong Standard-going profile (14 of 15 runs on similar going) and a win at this trip on this surface last time out (1/5f/STA); tongue-tie headgear noted, trainer in 0/3 over 14 days, and 52 days since last run warrants monitoring, but the course-and-distance form is compelling.|
runners_data.comment: Mick's Spirit has finished sixth in three of his last six starts and sits bottom of the rankings on our figures, making him hard to fancy here; he does at least have experience over today's trip and going, and was a winner five starts back.

runners_data.name: Lazzar
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has shown useful placed form at this trip on Good ground but has a thinner profile on Standard going (8/15 relevant runs); fresh on 13 days since last run and trainer in 0/2 over 14 days, and a shift to Polytrack from recent turf outings is a factor to weigh.|
runners_data.comment: Lazzar shaped with plenty of promise when second three starts back, and he returns on a quick turnaround having run over today's trip and going before, with our rating suggesting he holds more ability than his official mark of 66 implies; the concern is he has been winless in recent starts and must convert that latent promise.

runners_data.name: Style King
runners_data.note: In genuine form with 1-2-2 across his last three, all on Standard going at 6f; his natural style is prominent racing but with General Assembly and Desert Treasure both determined to lead, he is most likely to be bustled back from his preferred position — the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reflects a real risk that he races in a role that doesn't showcase his best.|
runners_data.comment: Rated below his official mark and ranked fifth of six on our figures, Style King makes the shortlist hard to build despite back-to-back second-place finishes and a win three starts back; he has experience over today's trip and going, and ten days since his last run suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Desert Treasure
runners_data.note: Top weight from a powerful stable (Haggas, 9/45 T14), but recent form reads 077 since two wins on Good ground, and his Standard-going record is untested in this sample; a genuine front-runner who needs to get his own way, and the presence of General Assembly makes that uncertain.|
runners_data.comment: Desert Treasure won back-to-back races four and five starts back, has experience over today's trip, and her rating puts her among the principals, but three winless efforts since those consecutive victories are the concern.

runners_data.name: Isle Of Lismore
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a sole win on Good ground (1/5f/GOO) but a deeply concerning Standard-going profile — 0 wins or places from 1 run on similar surface; visor headgear applied, 65 days since last run, and a genuinely late style means he needs significant pace collapse to reach his rivals in time over the minimum trip.|
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out and has previously handled today's trip and going, Isle Of Lismore arrives here in good heart and, despite 65 days off the track, makes plenty of appeal on his overall profile carrying 134 lb from stall six.

races.paceDynamic: General Assembly and Desert Treasure are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this minimum 5f trip on Lingfield's Polytrack, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a procession. That friction between two pace-setters is unlikely to produce a truly suicidal tempo on Standard going, but it will be honest and unrelenting enough to test those who cannot sustain effort through the final furlong. This race shape favours horses who can track just off a contested pace and pounce in the final 100 yards — prominent-to-midfield types who are not burning early reserves will be best placed. This field contains more pace and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position: Desert Treasure and General Assembly are most likely to actually lead, with Style King the runner most displaced from its natural prominent berth.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Grinds Out
scenarios.trigger: If Desert Treasure and General Assembly battle for supremacy and the pace holds true to the line, rewarding the horse that settles most economically just off the duel.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners press each other through the early stages, burning enough energy to leave the door ajar for a well-positioned tracker in the final furlong; horses racing with cover and relaxation through the first half of the race will arrive with most in reserve.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners edges clear early and sets a controlled solo lead, allowing a prominent horse to stalk and pounce close home.
scenarios.body: The pace resolves into a single leader with a clean gallop rather than a contested duel, suiting a horse who can sit a length or two off the pace and accelerate when the leader flattens out; the Standard surface at Lingfield rewards the well-held prominent runner on a sound surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closer Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the early duel proves severe enough to drain both front-runners through the final furlong, gifting a late finisher a clear winning run.
scenarios.body: Isle Of Lismore, racing from off the pace, would be the primary beneficiary if the leaders genuinely tie up inside the final 100 yards; however, this outcome is contingent on a sharper-than-expected contest up front and Isle Of Lismore's poor recent Standard-going profile (0 wins or places from 1 relevant run) limits confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners breaks sharply and establishes a clear, uncontested lead early, allowing them to control the pace and outstay rivals.
scenarios.body: Desert Treasure's two wins at this trip came when allowed to dictate unchallenged, and if General Assembly misses the break or concedes the early lead, the Haggas runner could coast to a straightforward win; the high weight (136lbs) and recent poor form (077) temper confidence in this outcome.

watchPoints.text: Desert Treasure and General Assembly will dispute the lead from the stalls — watch the first two furlongs closely to see whether one immediately concedes, as that determines whether the tempo is contested or controlled and reshapes every scenario.|

Style King is most vulnerable to being crowded out of his prominent position at the start given the number of pace-forward types; if he is pushed back behind the speed, his effective STYLE_FIT disadvantage becomes a live handicap on his chances.|

Isle Of Lismore has run once on Standard going without placing — watch whether the visor sharpens his early concentration and whether he gets a clear run from off the pace, as both conditions must be met for him to get competitive.|

Mick's Spirit's 52-day absence and trainer's 0/3 form over 14 days are worth tracking at the off; if he appears on his toes and travels well in the first furlong, the layoff concern diminishes quickly given his strong profile on this surface.|

General Assembly's two recent placed efforts on this exact surface and trip suggest he handles conditions well, but watch whether he is driven hard early in the duel with Desert Treasure — if he is visibly under pressure before halfway, his chance of staying on for a place evaporates.|

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Lady Aiyana
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer who will find herself racing closer to the pace than ideal in this overcrowded rear; sim-going figures are modest (0W2P) and the step to 1m2f on AW looks stretched — trainer has no wins from five starts over the fortnight.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a sixth, sixth, eighth and seventh preceding a runner-up effort last time, Lady Aiyana faces a stiff task from the bottom of the rankings, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a return to form last time out offers slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Pride Eye
runners_data.note: Solid AW course form (1W1P in sim-going) and a hold-up style that, unlike several rivals, has not been redistribution-mapped — Rob Hornby retains the ride and 9 days between runs is a straightforward preparation; the 1m2f trip here is longer than the bulk of her recent runs.
runners_data.comment: Pride Eye won one from six in recent starts and returns just nine days on, which keeps fitness ticking over, though consistency has been elusive with three top-five finishes offset by lesser efforts; she has run over today's trip and going before and carries 135 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Rogers Dream
runners_data.note: Course-experienced stayer whose form over 10f on Standard suits the trip, though the trainer's recent record reads 0 from 5 and the horse was last seen 27 days ago; naturally a hold-up performer who will be forced into a tighter berth than preferred given the compressed rear of this field.

runners_data.name: Senseofentitlement
runners_data.note: Six-year-old returning after 100 days off, which is a significant fitness concern, and the form string of 98-659 offers little encouragement; the horse wants to race out the back but will be pushed into midfield, compounding already slim credentials on ratings (OR 42, lowest in field).
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Senseofentitlement has been consistently out of the frame, with finishes no better than fifth in recent starts; 100 days off the track adds to the concern, though he has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Sharma d'Amour
runners_data.note: Placed twice on similar AW going (1W1P) and has a tidy piece of form — second at Goodwood — buried in the record; 110 days off is a question mark for trainer Coakley, but if fit and finding a clear run from midfield this is arguably the most interesting profile among the genuine hold-up types.
runners_data.comment: Sharma d'Amour was a solid second two starts back but has since slipped to a well-beaten ninth last time out, and 110 days off the track is a notable concern; she has run over today's trip and going, yet remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Sunset In Paris
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran who prefers to race off the pace but will be shuffled into the midfield mass; the Jenkins yard has produced a win from six in the last fortnight and the 50-day break is not alarming, yet the form figures of 99456 speak to a horse struggling to compete at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 11th of 13 on our figures, Sunset In Paris is hard to fancy despite having run over today's trip and going before; the 50-day absence adds another question mark for a gelding whose recent efforts have been going the wrong way.

runners_data.name: Taskheer
runners_data.note: Holds the best AW sim-going profile of any runner (13 from 15 runs on similar ground, 6 placed), wears a tongue-tie and is trained by Gary & Josh Moore who have hit form (2 wins from 21 starts recently); a natural hold-up type who is among the most likely of the redistributed group to push forward into a prominent berth — that makes him structurally well-placed for Scenario A and B.
runners_data.comment: Taskheer shaped with promise when third and second in recent starts, and has experience of today's distance and going, while our rating of 52 puts him right in contention; the main risk is a 72-day absence and winless recent form.

runners_data.name: Versatile
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have been over 16f at Goodwood, making this drop to 1m2f on AW a significant change of context; hold-up profile, Josephine Gordon rides, but the trip and surface combination is untested and the form at 16f barely translates — seven days since last run is fine.
runners_data.comment: Versatile refused on his latest start just seven days ago, which raises a significant question mark, and he has been winless in recent starts; experience over today's trip and going offers some encouragement, but the consistency of mid-to-rear finishes beforehand makes him hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Ernie McCrew
runners_data.note: The three-year-old carries a 7lb allowance advantage in a 135lb field, is lightly framed for this grade and showed a placed effort (second at Lingfield AW over 8f) in recent history; Millie Wonnacott claims 5lb, and while the trip is longer than anything attempted before, this horse's AW course exposure gives it a tactical edge over several rivals.
runners_data.comment: Ernie McCrew has been a model of consistency in recent starts, finishing second last time out after a string of placed and competitive efforts, and he has experience on today's going — the main concern is that he remains yet to win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Maryland Star
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has run at Lingfield AW over 12f (fifth, placed) and is a natural hold-up performer compelled to race in the midfield mass; J F Egan is a positive booking, but the form figures of 38057 are unremarkable and the 24-day freshener is straightforward at best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Maryland Star makes little appeal here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 24 days between runs leaves her reasonably fresh, but that is about as far as the case for her goes.

runners_data.name: Freedom Bay
runners_data.note: The lone pace-setter, redistributed from a prominent style to the front because no true front-runner exists in this field — wears tongue-tie and hood, which is notable equipment for a horse being asked to lead; the 2-10f GOO run (second) and 8f AW win suggest she has ability, and Callum Hutchinson will need to judge the gallop carefully to avoid being overhauled approaching the straight.
runners_data.comment: Consistent recent form makes Freedom Bay an appealing pick here — third two starts back and a winner three starts back, she arrives on a sound 24-day break with experience of today's trip and conditions, and her overall profile justifies the confidence from stall ten carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Iftikhaar
runners_data.note: 124 days off the track is the headline concern — the longest absence in the field — and the visor is retained from previous starts; placed twice at 10f on AW (including a Lingfield second) so the trip and surface suit, but returning from that lay-off in a 14-runner field asks plenty of trainer Jenkins.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Iftikhaar does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and his second four starts back offers a crumb of encouragement, though a 124-day absence and an unplaced latest run are clear negatives heading into this.

runners_data.name: Kaaress
runners_data.note: Wears a visor, has one AW win and one place from 15 similar-going starts, and is trained by Michael Attwater who has landed one winner from 17 recent runners; a hold-up type who, like Taskheer, is among those most likely to push forward and take a prominent position — that could be advantageous if the race shape unfolds on the pace.
runners_data.comment: Kaaress franked her recent form with a win six starts back and has experience of today's trip and going, while our rating ranks her clear of this field; the risk is a string of disappointing efforts in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Kev
runners_data.note: Tagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is a material concern in a 1m2f test with a compressed midfield; the form string of 09805 includes a blank and a non-completion, and being forced to race closer than natural only increases the likelihood of weakening late — Tom Marquand's class on the day may not be enough to overcome the profile's limitations here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Kev has run over today's going before and comes here fresh enough on a 15-day break, but a fifth last time out represents his best recent effort and an official rating of 48 leaves him with plenty to find against stronger rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Freedom Bay is the lone confirmed pace-setter, redistributed to the front from a prominent profile, and with no genuine natural front-runner in opposition she will dictate from the off at a rhythm entirely of her own choosing on Standard Lingfield AW over 1m2f. The remainder of the 14-runner field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types — Lady Aiyana, Rogers Dream, Senseofentitlement, Sunset In Paris, Taskheer, Maryland Star, Iftikhaar, Kaaress, and Kev are all true hold-up horses pushed into midfield positions on the map because there is simply insufficient room at the rear for all of them. Kaaress and Taskheer are the most likely of that group to push forward and contest a prominent berth, given their headgear (visor) and AW-specific form, but neither is a natural front-runner. The field holds far more hold-up types than can realistically obtain their preferred position, meaning many will race further forward than ideal and the tactical picture will be compressed in midfield. With Freedom Bay able to control fractions unopposed and the closers unable to all secure their natural ground, this race shape clearly favours the horse capable of tracking the pace from a handy position and sustaining a run — a prominent-to-midfield profile travelling within the contest is at a structural advantage over pure hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Freedom Bay Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Freedom Bay dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the hold-up pack cannot generate momentum from deep
scenarios.body: Freedom Bay sets a sustainable pace from the front and, crucially, no rival has the tactical speed or position to reel her in entering the straight; horses tracking her closely from second or third will be best placed as the compressed midfield struggles to produce a sustained late challenge from too far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sits second or third behind Freedom Bay throughout and produces a decisive move two furlongs out
scenarios.body: With the pace honest but not excessive, a horse camped just behind the leader will have cover, save ground and pounce when Freedom Bay ties up late; Taskheer and Kaaress, the two redistributed hold-up types most likely to push forward, are the natural beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Late Burst
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile and the compressed midfield produces one sustained finish
scenarios.body: Should Freedom Bay fade sharply and the race open up inside the final furlong, a horse with a clean passage through a crowded pack could emerge; however this scenario is structurally compromised because the true hold-up horses are racing out of role and will not find the deep-track position their style requires.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Freedom Bay quickens into the straight and simply does not come back to the field
scenarios.body: On Standard AW at Lingfield over 1m2f the front runner can get away from the field if the pace is well-judged and no rival has the tactical sharpness to go with her; with the field so backwardly drawn in terms of true running style, coordinated pursuit is unlikely to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Freedom Bay controls every dimension of this race — if she is allowed to roll along uncontested at a fair gallop, several rivals will be left flat-footed in the compressed midfield with no room to build a challenge; watch whether Taskheer or Kaaress push up to her girth early, as that could change the entire pace equation.

Kev is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish and is being raced out of role in a 14-runner midfield — if he gets outpaced and hampers the hold-up horses attempting to generate late momentum, the back-half of the field could cause interference at a crucial stage.

Senseofentitlement returns after 100 days without a run and is the lowest-rated horse in the field at OR 42; a lack of race fitness in a tightly bunched midfield could create traffic issues for those immediately behind.

Sharma d'Amour's 110-day absence is the second-longest in the race — monitor market moves close to post time; if the Denis Coakley yard has this horse primed, the AW placed form and sim-going credentials make it a more interesting runner than the odds may reflect.

Ernie McCrew's 3yo weight allowance (128lbs versus 135lbs for older rivals) is a tangible advantage in a flat handicap context — watch whether that 7lb edge translates in the market and whether the step up from 8f to 1m2f is treated as a positive or a concern by punters.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: King Cherry
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who sets his own fractions; Marco Ghiani knows this horse's habits, and with 7 days since his last run (recent campaign) and turf headgear applied, he controls whether this race is a test or a tactical crawl — his AW Standard sim-going record is modest (0W0P) but the uncontested lead changes everything.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, King Cherry has run over today's trip and going, arrives here just seven days on from his latest outing, and at 132 lb from stall 5, his profile on the day — fitness, conditions, and a rating of 70 — makes him our pick ahead of a stronger-looking field on paper.

runners_data.name: Twilight Baby
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who fades in the finish — Saffie Osborne must produce her late, but a 39-day break and a pattern of fading make this a tough ask; one placing in three runs at similar going and the "fades in finish" flag are real negatives in a race where closers need everything to fall right.
runners_data.comment: Showed a glimpse of ability with a third last time out, though eighth and ninth in the two runs prior give her profile a patchy look; has run over today's trip and going, but winless in recent starts and a stiff 132 lb from stall 12 leaves plenty to overcome.

runners_data.name: Ebn Sabt
runners_data.note: Ben Lund's 3yo has form at this trip on soft, but the key context is that he is a true rear-runner whose natural position is at the back — with this field so stacked with hold-up horses, he is likely to find himself hemmed in at midfield, racing without his preferred space; one win in fifteen at similar going adds further caution.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Ebn Sabt arrives here on a quick 14-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going in his favour, though his recent string of mid-to-rear finishes makes improvement hard to predict carrying 130 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Real Gold
runners_data.note: Rachel Cook & John Bridger's charge has shown consistent placing form (four places from thirteen similar-going runs) and handles AW Standard well enough, but operates best from the back and will almost certainly find traffic a recurring problem here given the congested hold-up contingent — the shorter trip compared to some recent efforts is also a factor.
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time out and winless in her last six starts, Real Gold does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, with four third-place finishes in that sequence suggesting she finds a way to be competitive without quite getting there.

runners_data.name: Lesley Buckley
runners_data.note: 58 days off the track is notable, the "fades in finish" flag is a structural concern, and she wears headgear (v); a true hold-up runner who has finished no better than third in her last five, all without a win — the lay-off and her tendency to weaken late make this very difficult in a race that may not produce the pace she needs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Lesley Buckley faces a stiff task, though she has experience of today's distance and going and a third two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement after 58 days off.

runners_data.name: Audere
runners_data.note: J F Egan is a quality booking, but Dean Ivory's runner has been knocking around in 6th-8th positions repeatedly across soft and AW ground; a natural hold-up type who will be jostling for space among several similar horses, with zero wins and a style-fit discount dragging down her chance in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Audere is hard to fancy, though she has run over today's trip and going before and 28 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Power Cut
runners_data.note: Chelsea Banham's 3yo has run exclusively on AW Standard going (all six career runs), which is track-specific experience that counts for something, but finishing positions of 5-8 across those starts without ever placing tells its own story — Joey Haynes will be looking for racing room that may simply not materialise.
runners_data.comment: Power Cut has been winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than fifth in recent outings, and his official rating of 45 makes him a tough sell against this field; the plus points are a quick turnaround of nine days suggesting he is fit, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Ruiz
runners_data.note: Simon Dow's horse drops back from 10f trips to 7f here, and his best run on AW Standard (3rd at 7f) came at this sort of distance — Tyler Heard rides, but as a true hold-up runner squeezed into the midfield cluster, he is racing out of his natural role; the step back in trip gives a modicum of optimism but the redistribution is a real check on expectations.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked last on our figures, Ruiz faces a stiff task here, though a run nine days ago leaves him fit and he has experience over today's distance and going, carrying 121 lb from stall two.

runners_data.name: Royal County Glory
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon's mount is the most dangerous prominent horse in the field behind King Cherry — one win and five places from twelve similar-going runs, and a win at 7f AW Standard last time, make this a genuine course-and-distance performer; the key question is whether he can maintain contact with King Cherry and use his engine in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Royal County Glory caught the eye with a runner-up finish last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating marking him as the standout in a field of twelve; the chief concern is that ninth two starts back hints at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Melodical
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand is a top booking for Ed Walker's 3yo, who has placed at this trip on Standard going; operating naturally from off the pace, Marquand will need a clean run and a genuinely testing pace to peg back any leader — 20 days since last run is fine, and the 7f trip suits better than 6f based on form.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back gives Melodical a case as a live threat, and she arrives fit on 20 days' rest with experience of today's distance and going; the main concern is a trainer firing at just 5% strike-rate over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Credit Forgedd It
runners_data.note: Sean Levey on Simon Dow's horse brings strong form at 7f on Good and AW going (2nd and 3rd twice in recent starts); a true hold-up type who has been finding the line well enough for places, and Levey's tactical awareness gives him the best chance of any closing horse threading through — the sim-going caution (6 from 12) is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Credit Forgedd It brings solid recent placing form — third two starts back and second three starts back — handles today's trip and going, and at 135 lb from stall eight looks a lively threat; the main concern is he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Irish Fusilier
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby takes the ride for Gary & Josh Moore on a horse returning from 83 days off, all previous form on soft ground — the going switch to AW Standard is a genuine unknown (no Standard form on record), and the layoff compounds the doubt; form figures of 9-4-5-7 include a solid 4th on Soft but this surface is uncharted territory.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning after 83 days off, Irish Fusilier faces a stiff ask from stall 11 carrying 135 lb, though he has run over today's trip before and a rating of 62 offers slim hope of improvement.

races.paceDynamic: King Cherry is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful pace rival to push him, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable tempo from the front at 7f on this flat Lingfield AW surface. Royal County Glory will press from a prominent position behind him, but is unlikely to force a genuine test — meaning King Cherry controls the fractions throughout. The field behind is overwhelmingly stacked with hold-up types (Ebn Sabt, Real Gold, Lesley Buckley, Audure, Power Cut, Ruiz, Melodical, Credit Forgedd It, Irish Fusilier), but the pace map cannot accommodate them all at the rear, and several — Ebn Sabt, Real Gold and Ruiz — are genuine hold-up horses remapped to midfield because there is simply not enough room at the back. With one front-runner setting a comfortable, unhurried pace and the hold-up contingent crowded and potentially boxed in, this race shape strongly favours the horse on the lead or sitting just off it in a prominent position, as closers face a compressed run with no true test to reel in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: King Cherry Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If King Cherry bowls along comfortably in front and Royal County Glory settles just off without applying pressure, setting a fair but not brutal tempo.
scenarios.body: King Cherry sets his own fractions, conserves energy through the middle section, and kicks clear in the final 2f before hold-up horses can organise a challenge; the flat, galloping nature of Lingfield AW at 7f suits a front-runner who can control pace rather than sprint.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Draw Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Royal County Glory tracks King Cherry aggressively and forces a slightly stronger pace, with the pair pulling clear of the hold-up pack.
scenarios.body: A contested lead between King Cherry and Royal County Glory lifts the gallop just enough that a hold-up horse with a good turn of foot can close late, but the prominent pair still dominate; runners who travel in the slipstream of a genuine two-way duel at the head of affairs benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If King Cherry either fades in the final furlong or the pace proves genuinely strong enough to set up a late closing run from the rear.
scenarios.body: Credit Forgedd It or Melodical, operating from a true hold-up position, get a clean run and pick off tired leaders in the closing stages; however, with so many hold-up horses remapped away from their natural position and traffic a near-certainty, this scenario is structurally unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If King Cherry is headed or voluntarily eases off and the race loses its shape entirely, creating a muddled sprint finish.
scenarios.body: With pace removed and the field bunching, a horse who can quicken from mid-division benefits from the scramble; horses tagged as redistributed midfield runners gain marginal relevance here, but their structural style-fit discount means this remains the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: King Cherry — if he gets to the front uncontested and Marco Ghiani settles him into a comfortable rhythm, the entire field is racing to catch a horse who controls the tempo; watch whether anything pushes him in the first 2f.

Traffic danger in the hold-up pack — with at least six genuine hold-up horses compressed into midfield, Credit Forgedd It, Melodical and Ruiz are all at risk of being boxed in turning for home; any horse drawn wide has a significant advantage in finding clear air.

Royal County Glory's position in the early stages is critical — if Cieren Fallon allows him to drift back rather than pressing King Cherry, he loses his structural advantage as the most natural prominent horse in the field.

Irish Fusilier — 83 days off and first run on AW Standard going for a horse with exclusively soft-ground form; watch the market and paddock closely, as Rob Hornby and the Moore stable are capable of producing a freshened horse fit to run well first time back.

Twilight Baby — the "fades in finish" flag combined with a 39-day break means Saffie Osborne will need to time her challenge to perfection; if the pace drops off and she hits the front too soon, the fade flag becomes a decisive liability.
